A Guy With A Scarf research/Automated match video/Premium edition/LiveBarn

Platform pays for cameras and shares revenue · adjacent platform

LiveBarnPremium

LiveBarn Inc. · Montreal, Quebec, Canada · founded 2015 · acquired · livebarn.com · last verified 2026-09-19

Platform pays for cameras and shares revenueSoftware onlyEvidence AViewer paysAdjacent platformAcquired by GTCR, closed April 2026

LiveBarn is a North American subscription network of fixed cameras installed free in more than 4,000 rinks, courts and fields, sold to families at $26.95 or $36.95 a month, and bought by GTCR for more than $400 million in April 2026 livebarn-01, livebarn-02, livebarn-03.

For Hockey families first, then parents in basketball, volleyball, swimming, baseball, soccer and other venue sports across 49 US states and 10 Canadian provinces, who pay one subscription to watch any game at any partner venue livebarn-02, livebarn-04. Venues join because the install and operation cost them nothing livebarn-04.

LiveBarn exists because indoor venues host thousands of games a week that nobody films, so it took the capital cost of fixed cameras onto its own balance sheet and sold the output as a Netflix-style subscription livebarn-01, livebarn-04. It matters now because the April 2026 sale to GTCR at more than $400 million, on estimated revenue of about $80 million, is the largest valuation marker yet for automated youth match video and GTCR has said it will expand from hockey into soccer, basketball, volleyball, baseball and swimming through its new Ascent Sports Group livebarn-02, livebarn-03, livebarn-05. It tells you that the venue-network subscription model, where the platform owns cameras and viewers and the club owns nothing, is what private equity is paying for, and that Europe has no equivalent at this scale livebarn-01, livebarn-02.

Price band Viewer subscription $26.95/month or $251.40/year (Basic) and $36.95/month or $347.40/year (Premium); free to venues livebarn-01

Italy LiveBarn operates in the United States and Canada only, with 49 states and 10 provinces covered and no European venues livebarn-02, livebarn-04.

The verdict

Look if You are a North American venue operator or league with heavy indoor traffic and want cameras installed at no cost with a subscriber audience already attached livebarn-04. You should also look at it as a benchmark if you are pricing a European venue-network or federation streaming service, since $26.95 a month for unlimited venues is the reference point private equity just underwrote livebarn-01, livebarn-02.

Skip if You are a club that wants to own its footage, its viewer relationship or a share of subscription revenue, since the LiveBarn model gives the venue free cameras and gives the club nothing livebarn-04. You should also skip it outside the US and Canada, where it does not operate livebarn-02.

Watch-outs

  • On-demand video is available for 30 days only and downloads are capped at 30 hours a month, so teams that want an archive must export in time livebarn-01.
  • Both plans carry identical features and the Premium tier's difference is not explained on the pricing page, so check what the extra $10 a month buys before choosing livebarn-01.
  • Public venue counts vary between more than 1,900 facilities at the January 2026 announcement and more than 4,000 venues at the April 2026 closing, which suggests different counting units livebarn-02, livebarn-03.
  • The founder and CEO Farrel Miller stepped down at closing and the new owner has stated ambitions to buy or build in other sports, so product priorities may shift under Ascent Sports Group livebarn-05.

Company

Ownership and funding LiveBarn Inc. was founded in 2015 in Montreal by Farrel Miller and was backed by Susquehanna Growth Equity and Ares before GTCR agreed on 23 January 2026 to acquire it for about $400 million as the first investment of its Ascent Sports Group, with Ares retaining a stake and providing financing; the deal closed on 7 April 2026 with former COO Ray Giroux as CEO and Miller moving to the Ascent board livebarn-02, livebarn-03, livebarn-05, livebarn-06.

Financials Private Equity Wire estimated annual revenue at around $80 million at the time of the deal livebarn-06. No audited figures are public.

Scale, company-stated More than 1,900 facilities in 49 US states and 10 Canadian provinces at the January 2026 announcement, and more than 4,000 venues at the April 2026 closing livebarn-02, livebarn-03. Cameras in 21 NHL team practice facilities according to the venue page livebarn-04.

Partnerships

  • NHL practice facilities for 21 teams including Toronto Maple Leafs, Winnipeg Jets and Ottawa Senators listed on the venue page livebarn-04.
  • GTCR's Ascent Sports Group, led by Gary Swidler, as the new holding company for youth sports assets livebarn-05.

2025 and 2026

  • 2026-01-23: GTCR agrees to acquire LiveBarn for about $400 million from Susquehanna Growth Equity and Ares livebarn-02, livebarn-06.
  • 2026-04-07: Acquisition completes, Ray Giroux named CEO, Farrel Miller joins the Ascent board, GTCR outlines expansion into baseball, basketball, soccer, volleyball and swimming livebarn-03, livebarn-05.

Not verified

  • Subscriber count and audited revenue.
  • The revenue share or other consideration paid to venues, which the venue page does not disclose.
  • What distinguishes the Premium plan from Basic, since the pricing page lists identical features.
  • The reason for the gap between 1,900 facilities and 4,000 venues in the two deal announcements.
